To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) discourse markers do signal rhetorical relations, but (b) not all relations are signalled by a discourse marker.

(1) the number of rhetorical relations that are signalled is much lower than the total number of relations in a discourse; (2) the number of relations that are not signalled is higher in conversation than in newspaper text; (3) the number of signalled relations is higher for some relations than for others.
(a) a high number of RST relations (between 70% and 60%) are not signalled, (b) genre-specific factors play a role in determining which relations are signaled.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether a discourse marker can be used as evidence for a particular rhetorical relation.
the question: how do writers (and speakers) signal rhetorical relations?

the question whether discourse markers can be used as signals of rhetorical relations, in a way that would be useful for the development of automatic text analysis tools, and the answer is that this is not the case.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
discourse markers are not reliable indicators of rhetorical relations.
there is no ‘right’ number, and that the presence or absence of signals should be taken into consideration when analysing a text.
the number of relations that are not signalled is higher than the number of relations signalled.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, while some relations can be signalled by specific discourse markers, the majority of them cannot, and that this is a genre-dependent fact.
discourse markers are not reliable signals of rhetorical relations.
discourse markers do not signal rhetorical relations in a one-to-one fashion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while discourse markers can provide a good approximation of the relations in a text, they are far from being a complete inventory.
discourse markers do not always signal the presence of a rhetorical relation.
the relation-to-signalling ratio is very different from what is assumed in RST and related frameworks.
